end.summary:
Matched everyday objects to cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones and spheres; this was shown on a why/new-situation question.
Recognised 3D shapes in different positions or sizes was practised; steadiness is still to check next time.
Naming cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere was practised; some names are still to check next time.
The cylinder-position mix-up was corrected later: a lying battery remains a cylinder because its circular ends remain circular.
end.parentNote: Asha practised matching everyday objects with cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere, using features such as flat or circular faces and pointed ends. Ishita gave clear reasons for the sphere, cone, cube and cuboid examples. There was a mix-up about a cylinder lying down, and Ishita corrected it later by noticing that its circular ends stay circular. At home, ask Ishita to name these five shapes using objects in the room, then turn one object around and ask whether its shape changes.
